skills.name: docx
skills.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

Use when creating architecture diagrams, flowcharts, data flow visualizations, or illustrations for proposals and design documents.

skills.name: expense-report

Handles travel expenses, recurring monthly expenses (internet, phone), hotel itemization, and corporate AMEX matching. Produces a complete, review-ready draft; the user always submits themselves. Triggers include: 'expense report', 'submit expense', 'file an expense', 'internet expense', 'monthly expense', 'travel expense', or any request to log a reimbursable cost.

skills.name: loop
skills.description: Edit Microsoft Loop documents in the browser using Playwright automation. Use when the user wants to create, edit, or update a Loop document, mentions 'Loop', 'Loop page', or 'Loop workspace', or wants to add content to a shared document in Loop.

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates, layouts, speaker notes, or comments; working with SharePoint-hosted or OneDrive-hosted presentations (even when no local file is involved). Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx filename or a SharePoint/OneDrive URL pointing to a presentation, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. IMPORTANT: If the input is a SharePoint or OneDrive URL, read ~/.copilot/skills/pptx/sharepoint.md before doing anything else.

skills.name: web-artifacts-builder
skills.description: Create interactive HTML artifacts (dashboards, visualizations, org charts, network maps, trackers, comparisons) as self-contained HTML files. Use whenever the user requests a web application, data visualization, interactive tool, or any HTML artifact. All output MUST use the Clawpilot theme variables defined in this skill. If the user will share the artifact or open it through OneDrive/SharePoint's in-browser preview, additionally follow the sandbox-safe rules in the "Sharing or previewing through OneDrive/SharePoint" section.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

9. Selection uses pytest **`-k` module selectors**, NOT file paths: the black-box
10. `xcvrd-tests/run.sh` always runs `pytest <tests-dir> <extra args>`, so passing file
11. paths would either collect the whole dir or error on a relative path. A `-k
12. "test_presence or test_info_content"` expression narrows the already-collected dir
13. to exactly the intended modules (matched by the test module stem in each node id).
14. 
15. Every milestone runs its FULL cumulative module set, **including slow tests** (no
16. `-m` marker filter). Earlier the inner loop filtered `-m "not slow"` for speed;
17. now correctness at each milestone is checked against the slow tests too.
18. """

20. 
21. from dataclasses import dataclass, field
22. 
23. DEFAULT_MARKER = ""   # no pytest -m filter: run slow tests at every milestone
24. 
25.

32.     marker: str = DEFAULT_MARKER                 # pytest -m marker for the (cumulative) run
33. 
34.

43.     ),

49.     ),

52.         "Periodically poll module monitors via the platform and publish "
53.         "TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR; the emulator Monitor trace shows real reads.",
54.         test_modules=["test_dom", "test_interaction_trace"],
55.     ),

57.         "M3", "Status / CMIS state / errors",
58.         "Publish TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW (plug status, cmis_state=READY) and decode "
59.         "injected error events (blocking removes DOM, non-blocking keeps it).",
60.         test_modules=["test_status_error"],
61.     ),
62.     Milestone(

64.         "Handle sfputil lpmode/reset: drive the CMIS ModuleGlobalControls writes "
65.         "and reflect lpmode state.",
66.         test_modules=["test_lpmode_reset"],
67.     ),
68.     Milestone(
69.         "M5", "Multiport concurrency",
70.         "Handle concurrent presence/DOM across many ports with per-module "
71.         "isolation (no cross-talk).",
72.         test_modules=["test_multiport"],
73.     ),
74.     Milestone(

76.         "Reproduce the reference STATE_DB projection and pass the ENTIRE suite, "
77.         "including slow tests (no marker filter).",
78.         test_modules=["test_golden"], marker="",   # full suite incl. slow
79.     ),
80. ]
81. 
82. 
83. def index_of(mid: str) -> int:
84.     for i, m in enumerate(MILESTONES):
85.         if m.id == mid:
86.             return i
87.     raise KeyError(mid)

89.

92. 
93.

95.     """The test module stems for a milestone's cumulative gate (M1..mid), in order."""
96.     idx = index_of(mid)
97.     mods: list[str] = []
98.     for m in MILESTONES[1:idx + 1]:              # M1..current
99.         for mod in m.test_modules:
100.             if mod not in mods:
101.                 mods.append(mod)
102.     return mods
103. 
104. 
105. def cumulative_args(mid: str) -> list[str]:
106.     """pytest args for a milestone's CUMULATIVE gate: a `-k` expression selecting
107.     this milestone's modules plus every earlier milestone's, plus the current
108.     milestone's `-m` marker. M0 returns [] (deploy-smoke; no pytest)."""
109.     mods = cumulative_modules(mid)
110.     if not mods:

112.     args = ["-k", " or ".join(mods)]
113.     marker = MILESTONES[index_of(mid)].marker
114.     if marker:
115.         args += ["-m", marker]
116.     return args

122.     import sys

130.         print(f"     gate: {' '.join(cumulative_args(m.id)) or '(deploy-smoke)'}")
131.     return 0
132. 
133. 
134. if __name__ == "__main__":
135.     raise SystemExit(_cli())

1. # Analyzer Design Document — SONiC `xcvrd` Python → Rust
2. 
3. > ReCodeAgent (arXiv:2604.07341 §3.2) Analyzer output. Three parts, mirroring
4. > Figure 5: **(1) Source Project Research**, **(2) Third‑Party Library Analysis**,
5. > **(3) Target Project Design**. The Planner/Translator/Validator agents treat
6. > Part 3 as authoritative.
7. >
8. > **Hard project constraints baked in below** (README §2–§3): thick HAL via
9. > `platform-bridge` (PyO3 → `sonic_platform`); STATE_DB via `swss-common`;
10. > two validation layers (Rust mocked unit tests **+** the immutable `xcvrd-tests`
11. > black‑box oracle); mirror the Python package layout in Rust; extend the M1
12. > bootstrap in `crate/xcvrd-rs/` (never edit `crate/`; work in `pipeline/crate/`).
13. > **This document writes no Rust.**
14. 
15. ---
16. 
17. # Part 1 — Source Project Research
18. 
19. ## 1.1 Overview
20. 
21. `xcvrd` is SONiC's **transceiver information update daemon**. It runs in the
22. `pmon` container, discovers pluggable optics (SFP/QSFP/QSFP‑DD/OSFP) through the
23. platform HAL, and continuously projects their state into Redis **STATE_DB** so
24. the rest of SONiC (CLI, SNMP, telemetry, orchagent) sees a live view of every
25. optic. It also drives module bring‑up (CMIS datapath init) and applies host SI /
26. media settings.
27. 
28. The entrypoint is `main()` in `source/xcvrd/xcvrd.py`, which builds a
29. **`DaemonXcvrd(daemon_base.DaemonBase)`** and calls `run()`. `DaemonXcvrd.init()`
30. loads the platform chassis (`sonic_platform.platform.Platform().get_chassis()`),
31. waits for port config, builds the logical↔physical **port mapping** from
32. CONFIG_DB, and cleans stale rows. `DaemonXcvrd.run()` then spawns a set of
33. **task threads** and blocks on `stop_event` (`xcvrd.py:1142‑1236`):
34. 
35. | Thread (class) | File | Responsibility | Enabled |
36. |---|---|---|---|
37. | **`SfpStateUpdateTask`** | `xcvrd.py:259` | The core: presence/hot‑plug event loop; publishes `TRANSCEIVER_INFO` + `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`, DOM/VDM thresholds on insert, decodes error events, deletes rows on removal | always |
38. | **`CmisManagerTask`** | `cmis/cmis_manager_task.py:41` | CMIS datapath state machine (INSERTED→…→READY); writes `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW.cmis_state`; configures app‑sel, tx power, laser freq | unless `--skip_cmis_mgr` |
39. | **`DomInfoUpdateTask`** | `dom/dom_mgr.py:141` | ~60 s poll of DOM sensors, HW status, DOM/status **flags**, VDM, PM, firmware; publishes `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR`, `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS`, etc. | always |
40. | **`DomThermalInfoUpdateTask`** | `dom/dom_mgr.py:526` | Faster module‑temperature poll into `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_TEMPERATURE` | if `--dom_temperature_poll_interval` |
41. | **`SffManagerTask`** | `sff_mgr.py:45` | Non‑CMIS (SFF‑8636) TX enable/disable + high‑power‑class from `host_tx_ready`/`admin_status` | only if `--enable_sff_mgr` |
42. 
43. Stimulus comes from the HAL: `chassis.get_change_event(timeout)` returns
44. plug/unplug/error events, and each `sfp.get_transceiver_*()` reads and CMIS/SFF‑
45. decodes the module EEPROM. On the testbed the HAL is the `sonic_platform` plugin
46. that speaks gRPC to the **`xcvr-emu`** emulator.
47. 
48. > **Local snapshot vs. upstream.** `source/xcvrd/` is a **modular refactor** of
49. > upstream `sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/sonic-xcvrd`: DOM logic is split into
50. > `dom/` (a `DomInfoUpdateTask` + `dom/utilities/{db,dom_sensor,status,vdm}`),
51. > and CMIS into `cmis/`. The upstream **behavioral unit tests**
52. > (`source/xcvrd/tests/test_xcvrd.py`) are largely from `master`, so some map
53. > straight onto the refactored modules and some must become **new** Rust tests
54. > (called out in §3.6). The **`xcvrd-tests/`** black‑box suite is snapshot‑
55. > independent — it only asserts STATE_DB.
56. 
57. ## 1.2 Directory structure (`source/xcvrd/`)
58. 
59. ```

113. `PortChangeObserver` (`:46`) subscribes to CONFIG_DB/APPL_DB `PORT` changes at
114. runtime. **On the testbed the mapping is `Ethernet{index*4}` ↔ `index`**

118. ### 1.3.3 `SfpStateUpdateTask` — the core loop (`xcvrd.py:395‑693`)
119. `init()` posts all present ports' info + DOM/VDM thresholds once
120. (`_post_port_sfp_info_and_dom_thr_to_db_once`) and seeds `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`
121. (`_init_port_sfp_status_sw_tbl`). `task_worker` runs an **INIT/NORMAL/EXIT state
122. machine** over `get_change_event`. Per physical port event code `value`:
123. * `'1'` (`SFP_STATUS_INSERTED`) → `STATUS_SW.status='1'`, `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` (retry once on `SFP_EEPROM_NOT_READY`), then post DOM/VDM thresholds + media settings.
124. * `'0'` (`SFP_STATUS_REMOVED`) → `STATUS_SW.status='0'`, `del_port_sfp_dom_info_from_db` across INFO/DOM/STATUS/VDM/PM/FW tables.
125. * other (error bitmap) → decode → `STATUS_SW.error='|'.join(descriptions)`; if blocking bit set, delete DOM tables (keep static INFO).

127. ### 1.3.4 `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` (`xcvrd.py:178`)
128. For a present port, take `get_transceiver_info()`; **if `cmis_rev` present** write
129. **every** field as `str(value)` plus `is_replaceable` (the CMIS branch — the case
130. on this testbed); else write the fixed SFF field list. This exact behavior is
131. already reproduced by the bootstrap `sync_port` (`crate/xcvrd-rs/src/daemon.rs`).

134. Every `dom_update_interval` (default **60 s**), for each physical port not in

136. DOM flags, HW status, HW status flags, and (if VDM supported) VDM real values +
137. flags + PM. The generic write path is `DBUtils.post_diagnostic_values_to_db`
138. (`dom/utilities/db/utils.py:19`): read a `{field:value}` dict from the SFP,
139. `beautify` (stringify / strip units), append `last_update_time`, `table.set`.

180. Cross‑referenced against `xcvrd-tests/tests/*` and `lib/golden.py`:
181. 
182. * **`TRANSCEIVER_INFO`** — populated iff present; cleared on unplug; `manufacturer=="xcvr-emu"`, `model=="EMU-40G-LR4"`, `vendor_oui=="01-02-03"`, `serial=="0123456789"`, `vendor_rev in ("01","1")`, `type` contains `QSFP`+`DD`, `ext_identifier` contains `"Power Class 8"` (`test_info_content.py`, `test_presence.py`).

184. * **`TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR`** — has `temperature` & `voltage`; a raw emulator write propagates after the ~60 s refresh (`test_dom.py`).
185. * **Blocking error** removes `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR` but keeps `TRANSCEIVER_INFO`; **non‑blocking** keeps DOM (`test_status_error.py`).
186. * **Golden (M6)** — exact match of the projection `{TRANSCEIVER_INFO, TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW, TRANSCEIVER_DOM_THRESHOLD}` (minus volatile `last_update_time`) vs. `xcvrd-tests/golden/Ethernet100.json`. That file is the **canonical field list** for M1/M2/M3 outputs (e.g. `TRANSCEIVER_INFO` = `active_apsel_hostlane1..8, application_advertisement, cable_length, cable_type, cmis_rev, connector, encoding, ext_identifier, ext_rateselect_compliance, hardware_rev, host_lane_count, is_replaceable, manufacturer, media_interface_technology, media_lane_count, model, nominal_bit_rate, serial, specification_compliance, type, type_abbrv_name, vdm_supported, vendor_date, vendor_oui, vendor_rev`; `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW` = `{cmis_state:READY, error:N/A, status:1}`; `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_THRESHOLD` = 24 temp/vcc/tx/rx/laser threshold fields).
187. * **Interaction trace** — xcvrd must actually **read** the EEPROM (emulator `Monitor` stream): steady‑state reads + a ≥3‑read burst after re‑plug + page‑00h reads (`test_interaction_trace.py`). This means the Rust daemon must genuinely poll via the bridge, not cache.
188. * **lpmode/reset** — driven through `sfputil`/the bridge, **not** through the Rust daemon: `reset`→`00h:26=0x08`, `lpmode on`→`0x10` on the Monitor trace (`test_lpmode_reset.py`). See §3.7 M4.

190. ## 1.5 Error handling
191. 
192. * **Absent module:** `_wrapper_get_presence` false → `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` skips; on a removal event `del_port_sfp_dom_info_from_db` wipes the port's rows and `STATUS_SW.status='0'`. `remove_stale_transceiver_info` (`xcvrd.py:986`) clears INFO for absent ports at boot.
193. * **Hardware/EEPROM errors (SfpBase bitmaps):** `sfp_status_helper.py` — `SFP_ERRORS_BLOCKING_MASK=0x02`, `SFP_ERRORS_GENERIC_MASK=0x0000FFFE`, `SFP_ERRORS_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_MASK=0xFFFF0000`. `fetch_generic_error_description` maps bits via `SfpBase.SFP_ERROR_BIT_TO_DESCRIPTION_DICT`; blocking (`is_error_block_eeprom_reading`) → drop DOM. Event codes: `'1'`/`'0'` are insert/remove, anything else is an error bitmap. `xcvrd-tests/lib/errors.py` enumerates the same bits/descriptions the oracle expects (`"Bus stuck (I2C data or clock shorted)"`, `"Bad or unsupported EEPROM"`, `"High temperature"`, blocking `"Blocking EEPROM from being read"`).
194. * **`NotImplementedError`:** pervasive `try/except NotImplementedError` → treat as "feature absent" (skip / empty dict). `NOT_IMPLEMENTED_ERROR=3` causes `sys.exit` only in the info/firmware post paths.
195. * **Threading/shutdown:** signals in `DaemonXcvrd.signal_handler` (SIGINT/SIGTERM set `stop_event`, SIGHUP re‑reads log level); a fatal `SfpStateUpdateTask` state → `os.kill(getppid(), SIGTERM)`; child‑thread exceptions escalate to `SIGKILL`; `sfp_error_event` → `sys.exit(SFP_SYSTEM_ERROR=4)`.

 # Part 1 — Source Project Research
 
 ## 1.1 Overview
 
 `xcvrd` is SONiC's **transceiver information update daemon**. It runs in the
 `pmon` container, discovers pluggable optics (SFP/QSFP/QSFP‑DD/OSFP) through the
 platform HAL, and continuously projects their state into Redis **STATE_DB** so
 the rest of SONiC (CLI, SNMP, telemetry, orchagent) sees a live view of every
 optic. It also drives module bring‑up (CMIS datapath init) and applies host SI /
 media settings.
 
 The entrypoint is `main()` in `source/xcvrd/xcvrd.py`, which builds a
 **`DaemonXcvrd(daemon_base.DaemonBase)`** and calls `run()`. `DaemonXcvrd.init()`
 loads the platform chassis (`sonic_platform.platform.Platform().get_chassis()`),
 waits for port config, builds the logical↔physical **port mapping** from
 CONFIG_DB, and cleans stale rows. `DaemonXcvrd.run()` then spawns a set of
 **task threads** and blocks on `stop_event` (`xcvrd.py:1142‑1236`):
 
 | Thread (class) | File | Responsibility | Enabled |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | **`SfpStateUpdateTask`** | `xcvrd.py:259` | The core: presence/hot‑plug event loop; publishes `TRANSCEIVER_INFO` + `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`, DOM/VDM thresholds on insert, decodes error events, deletes rows on removal | always |
 | **`CmisManagerTask`** | `cmis/cmis_manager_task.py:41` | CMIS datapath state machine (INSERTED→…→READY); writes `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW.cmis_state`; configures app‑sel, tx power, laser freq | unless `--skip_cmis_mgr` |
 | **`DomInfoUpdateTask`** | `dom/dom_mgr.py:141` | ~60 s poll of DOM sensors, HW status, DOM/status **flags**, VDM, PM, firmware; publishes `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR`, `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS`, etc. | always |
 | **`DomThermalInfoUpdateTask`** | `dom/dom_mgr.py:526` | Faster module‑temperature poll into `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_TEMPERATURE` | if `--dom_temperature_poll_interval` |
 | **`SffManagerTask`** | `sff_mgr.py:45` | Non‑CMIS (SFF‑8636) TX enable/disable + high‑power‑class from `host_tx_ready`/`admin_status` | only if `--enable_sff_mgr` |
 
 Stimulus comes from the HAL: `chassis.get_change_event(timeout)` returns
 plug/unplug/error events, and each `sfp.get_transceiver_*()` reads and CMIS/SFF‑
 decodes the module EEPROM. On the testbed the HAL is the `sonic_platform` plugin
 that speaks gRPC to the **`xcvr-emu`** emulator.
 
 > **Local snapshot vs. upstream.** `source/xcvrd/` is a **modular refactor** of
 > upstream `sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons/sonic-xcvrd`: DOM logic is split into
 > `dom/` (a `DomInfoUpdateTask` + `dom/utilities/{db,dom_sensor,status,vdm}`),
 > and CMIS into `cmis/`. The upstream **behavioral unit tests**
 > (`source/xcvrd/tests/test_xcvrd.py`) are largely from `master`, so some map
 > straight onto the refactored modules and some must become **new** Rust tests
 > (called out in §3.6). The **`xcvrd-tests/`** black‑box suite is snapshot‑

 ### 1.3.2 Port mapping (logical ↔ physical), `port_event_helper.py:212`
 `PortMapping` holds four dicts: `logical_port_list`, `logical_to_physical`
 (`Ethernet100`→`25`), `physical_to_logical` (`25`→`[Ethernet100,…]`, natsorted),
 `logical_to_asic`. Built by `get_port_mapping(namespaces)` (`:346`) which scans
 CONFIG_DB `PORT` and emits `PortChangeEvent(key, fvp['index'], asic, PORT_ADD)`.
 `PortChangeObserver` (`:46`) subscribes to CONFIG_DB/APPL_DB `PORT` changes at
 runtime. **On the testbed the mapping is `Ethernet{index*4}` ↔ `index`**
 (`xcvrd-tests/lib/emu.py:port_to_index`, and the bootstrap `discover_ports` in
 `crate/xcvrd-rs/src/daemon.rs`).
 
 ### 1.3.3 `SfpStateUpdateTask` — the core loop (`xcvrd.py:395‑693`)
 `init()` posts all present ports' info + DOM/VDM thresholds once
 (`_post_port_sfp_info_and_dom_thr_to_db_once`) and seeds `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`
 (`_init_port_sfp_status_sw_tbl`). `task_worker` runs an **INIT/NORMAL/EXIT state
 machine** over `get_change_event`. Per physical port event code `value`:
 * `'1'` (`SFP_STATUS_INSERTED`) → `STATUS_SW.status='1'`, `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` (retry once on `SFP_EEPROM_NOT_READY`), then post DOM/VDM thresholds + media settings.
 * `'0'` (`SFP_STATUS_REMOVED`) → `STATUS_SW.status='0'`, `del_port_sfp_dom_info_from_db` across INFO/DOM/STATUS/VDM/PM/FW tables.
 * other (error bitmap) → decode → `STATUS_SW.error='|'.join(descriptions)`; if blocking bit set, delete DOM tables (keep static INFO).
 
 ### 1.3.4 `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` (`xcvrd.py:178`)
 For a present port, take `get_transceiver_info()`; **if `cmis_rev` present** write
 **every** field as `str(value)` plus `is_replaceable` (the CMIS branch — the case
 on this testbed); else write the fixed SFF field list. This exact behavior is
 already reproduced by the bootstrap `sync_port` (`crate/xcvrd-rs/src/daemon.rs`).
 
 ### 1.3.5 DOM poll loop `DomInfoUpdateTask.task_worker` (`dom/dom_mgr.py:284`)
 Every `dom_update_interval` (default **60 s**), for each physical port not in
 error and present: post firmware info, `post_port_dom_sensor_info_to_db`,
 DOM flags, HW status, HW status flags, and (if VDM supported) VDM real values +
 flags + PM. The generic write path is `DBUtils.post_diagnostic_values_to_db`
 (`dom/utilities/db/utils.py:19`): read a `{field:value}` dict from the SFP,
 `beautify` (stringify / strip units), append `last_update_time`, `table.set`.
 Flag tables additionally maintain change‑count / set‑time / clear‑time metadata
 (`_update_flag_metadata_tables`).
 
 ### 1.3.6 `CmisManagerTask` (`cmis/cmis_manager_task.py`)
 The most complex module: a per‑lport CMIS **datapath state machine**
 (`process_cmis_state_machine`, states `CMIS_STATE_*` in `common.py:22‑39`:
 `INSERTED, DP_PRE_INIT_CHECK, DP_DEINIT, AP_CONFIGURED, DP_INIT, DP_TXON, READY,
 REMOVED, FAILED`). It sets `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW.cmis_state`
 (`update_port_transceiver_status_table_sw_cmis_state:85`). `process_single_lport`
 (`:1247`) short‑circuits to **`READY`** for non‑CMIS / flat‑memory / no‑api
 modules, and computes app‑sel/host‑lane masks otherwise. **Observable contract
 for the oracle is only `cmis_state == "READY"`** (see §1.5) — the emulator module
 reaches datapath‑up, so a much‑reduced state machine can satisfy the tests
 (§3.7, M3).
 
 ### 1.3.7 STATE_DB table handles `XcvrTableHelper` (`xcvr_table_helper.py:55`)
 Central registry that opens one `swsscommon.Table` per TRANSCEIVER_* table per
 ASIC (list in §1.4). Getters like `get_intf_tbl(asic)`, `get_dom_tbl`,
 `get_status_sw_tbl`, `get_dom_threshold_tbl` are used throughout.
 
 ## 1.4 Data models — STATE_DB schema xcvrd produces
 
 Table names are constants in `xcvr_table_helper.py:11‑47`; keys are the **logical
 port** (`Ethernet100`), i.e. Redis hash key `"<TABLE>|<lport>"`.
 
 | Table | Written by | Source method | Milestone |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | **`TRANSCEIVER_INFO`** | SfpStateUpdate | `get_transceiver_info()` (+`is_replaceable`) | **M1** |
 | **`TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`** | SfpStateUpdate (`status`,`error`) + Cmis (`cmis_state`) | `update_port_transceiver_status_table_sw` `common.py:110`; cmis `:85` | **M1/M3** |
 | **`TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR`** | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_dom_real_value()` | **M2** |
 | **`TRANSCEIVER_DOM_THRESHOLD`** | SfpStateUpdate on insert | `get_transceiver_threshold_info()` | **M2/M6** |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_TEMPERATURE` | DomThermal | `get_temperature()` | (opt) |
 | **`TRANSCEIVER_STATUS`** | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_status()` | M3/M6 |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_FLAG` (+`_CHANGE_COUNT`/`_SET_TIME`/`_CLEAR_TIME`) | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_dom_flags()` | later |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_FLAG` (+metadata trio) | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_status_flags()` | later |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_VDM_{HALARM,LALARM,HWARN,LWARN}_{THRESHOLD,FLAG,…}`, `TRANSCEIVER_VDM_REAL_VALUE` | Sfp/Dom + VDMDBUtils | VDM api | later |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_PM` | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_pm()` | later |
 | `TRANSCEIVER_FIRMWARE_INFO` | DomInfoUpdate | `get_transceiver_firmware_info()` | later |
 
 ### The oracle contract (what `xcvrd-tests` actually asserts)
 Cross‑referenced against `xcvrd-tests/tests/*` and `lib/golden.py`:
 
 * **`TRANSCEIVER_INFO`** — populated iff present; cleared on unplug; `manufacturer=="xcvr-emu"`, `model=="EMU-40G-LR4"`, `vendor_oui=="01-02-03"`, `serial=="0123456789"`, `vendor_rev in ("01","1")`, `type` contains `QSFP`+`DD`, `ext_identifier` contains `"Power Class 8"` (`test_info_content.py`, `test_presence.py`).
 * **`TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW`** — `status`=`"1"`/`"0"` with plug state; `cmis_state=="READY"` when present; `error` set to decoded description(s) on injected error, back to `"N/A"` on recovery (`test_presence.py`, `test_status_error.py`).
 * **`TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR`** — has `temperature` & `voltage`; a raw emulator write propagates after the ~60 s refresh (`test_dom.py`).
 * **Blocking error** removes `TRANSCEIVER_DOM_SENSOR` but keeps `TRANSCEIVER_INFO`; **non‑blocking** keeps DOM (`test_status_error.py`).
 * **Golden (M6)** — exact match of the projection `{TRANSCEIVER_INFO, TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW, TRANSCEIVER_DOM_THRESHOLD}` (minus volatile `last_update_time`) vs. `xcvrd-tests/golden/Ethernet100.json`.  * **lpmode/reset** — driven through `sfputil`/the bridge, **not** through the Rust daemon: `reset`→`00h:26=0x08`, `lpmode on`→`0x10` on the Monitor trace (`test_lpmode_reset.py`). See §3.7 M4.
 
 ## 1.5 Error handling
 
 * **Absent module:** `_wrapper_get_presence` false → `post_port_sfp_info_to_db` skips; on a removal event `del_port_sfp_dom_info_from_db` wipes the port's rows and `STATUS_SW.status='0'`. `remove_stale_transceiver_info` (`xcvrd.py:986`) clears INFO for absent ports at boot.
 * **Hardware/EEPROM errors (SfpBase bitmaps):** `sfp_status_helper.py` — `SFP_ERRORS_BLOCKING_MASK=0x02`, `SFP_ERRORS_GENERIC_MASK=0x0000FFFE`, `SFP_ERRORS_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_MASK=0xFFFF0000`. `fetch_generic_error_description` maps bits via `SfpBase.SFP_ERROR_BIT_TO_DESCRIPTION_DICT`; blocking (`is_error_block_eeprom_reading`) → drop DOM. Event codes: `'1'`/`'0'` are insert/remove, anything else is an error bitmap. `xcvrd-tests/lib/errors.py` enumerates the same bits/descriptions the oracle expects (`"Bus stuck (I2C data or clock shorted)"`, `"Bad or unsupported EEPROM"`, `"High temperature"`, blocking `"Blocking EEPROM from being read"`).
 * **`NotImplementedError`:** pervasive `try/except NotImplementedError` → treat as "feature absent" (skip / empty dict). `NOT_IMPLEMENTED_ERROR=3` causes `sys.exit` only in the info/firmware post paths.
 * **Threading/shutdown:** signals in `DaemonXcvrd.signal_handler` (SIGINT/SIGTERM set `stop_event`, SIGHUP re‑reads log level); a fatal `SfpStateUpdateTask` state → `os.kill(getppid(), SIGTERM)`; child‑thread exceptions escalate to `SIGKILL`; `sfp_error_event` → `sys.exit(SFP_SYSTEM_ERROR=4)`.

 ## 1.7 Unit tests (`source/xcvrd/tests/`)

   (`mock_platform.py` itself only mocks chassis/fans/thermals — SFP mocking is

248. # Part 2 — Third‑Party Library Analysis
249. 
250. Format per dependency: **Overview · How xcvrd uses it · Rust recommendation**.
251. The decisive question is *which needs are already met by the provided scaffolding*
252. so the Translator does **not** reinvent interop.
253. 
254. ### 2.1 `sonic_platform` plugin + `sonic_platform_base` (CMIS/SFF decode, gRPC)
255. * **Overview:** the platform HAL. `Sfp(SfpOptoeBase)` turns raw EEPROM into the
256.   full transceiver API (`get_transceiver_info/_dom_real_value/_status/_threshold_info`,
257.   lpmode/reset via `CmisApi`); `Chassis` gives `get_num_sfps/get_sfp/get_change_event`.
258. * **xcvrd use:** every HW read/write and every plug/error event.
259. * **Rust recommendation — ALREADY MET by `crate/platform-bridge` (PyO3 → the real
260.   plugin).** `platform_bridge::{Platform, Chassis, Sfp, ChangeEvent}` expose the
261.   exact surface as typed methods (scalars) and `serde_json::Value` (dicts). **Do
262.   NOT** port CMIS/SFF decode, gRPC, or `emu_client` to Rust — it stays in Python
263.   behind the bridge (README §3a; proven on the DUT). No new crate.
264. 
265. ### 2.2 `swsscommon` (Redis STATE_DB / CONFIG_DB / APPL_DB)
266. * **Overview:** SONiC's C++ DB access lib (`Table`, `ProducerStateTable`,
267.   `SubscriberStateTable`, `Select`, `FieldValuePairs`, `SonicDBConfig`).
268. * **xcvrd use:** all STATE_DB writes; CONFIG_DB `PORT` reads for port mapping;
269.   APPL_DB `PORT_TABLE` subscription for `wait_for_port_config_done` and DOM link
270.   events.
271. * **Rust recommendation — ALREADY MET by the official `swss-common` crate**
272.   (pinned git rev `7faca59…` in `crate/xcvrd-rs/Cargo.toml`), exposing
273.   `DbConnector`, `Table`, `ProducerStateTable`, `SubscriberStateTable`. Bootstrap
274.   uses `DbConnector::new_unix(6, "/var/run/redis/redis.sock", 0)?.hset(key, field,
275.   &CxxString::from(v))` (see `env.rs`, both `examples/`). Use `Table` for
276.   table‑scoped `set`/`del` where it mirrors the Python `XcvrTableHelper` closely.
277.   No new crate; no hand‑rolled Redis client.
278. 
279. ### 2.3 `sonic_py_common` — `daemon_base`, `syslogger`/`logger`, `multi_asic`
280. * **Overview:** `DaemonBase` (signals, plugin loading, `db_connect`), a syslog
281.   logger, and multi‑ASIC namespace helpers.
282. * **xcvrd use:** `DaemonXcvrd(daemon_base.DaemonBase)`, logging everywhere,
283.   `multi_asic.get_front_end_namespaces()` / `get_asic_index_from_namespace`.
284. * **Rust recommendation:**
285.   * *DaemonBase lifecycle* → **std**: the M0/M1 bootstrap already runs under the
286.     pmon supervisor via a Python shim (README §6); implement signals with the
287.     **`signal-hook`** crate (or a `ctrlc` handler) writing an `AtomicBool`/channel.
288.   * *Logging* → **`log`** + **`env_logger`** (or `syslog` crate) — the bootstrap
289.     currently uses `eprintln!`, which supervisor captures; a `log` facade is the
290.     idiomatic upgrade. Small, std‑adjacent; acceptable NEW deps.
291.   * *multi‑ASIC* → **out of scope for the testbed** (single ASIC, namespace `""`,
292.     `STATE_DB=6`/`CONFIG_DB=4` in `env.rs`). Model `asic_id` as a constant `0`;
293.     keep a `namespaces: Vec<String>` seam for fidelity but don't build multi‑ASIC.
294. 
295. ### 2.4 `natsort.natsorted`
296. * **Overview/use:** natural sort of logical ports sharing a physical port
297.   (`PortMapping._handle_port_add`).
298. * **Rust recommendation:** trivial — the **`natord`** crate, or a hand‑rolled
299.   natural comparator. On the testbed each physical port has exactly one logical
300.   port, so plain sort suffices; add `natord` only if breakout ports are modeled.
301. 
302. ### 2.5 Python stdlib (`threading`, `time`/`datetime`, `json`, `re`, `argparse`, `subprocess`, `signal`, `copy`)

1. //! xcvrd-rs daemon entrypoint.
2. //!
3. //! Runs the M1 bootstrap (presence + identity): populate TRANSCEIVER_INFO /
4. //! TRANSCEIVER_STATUS_SW for present transceivers and react to plug/unplug, so the
5. //! black-box suite gets past the clean-baseline fixture and the M1 tests actually
6. //! run. The logic lives in `xcvrd_rs::daemon` (built on the platform-bridge HAL +
7. //! swss-common STATE_DB bindings); the translation agents extend it milestone by
8. //! milestone. See the crate lib docs + `examples/` for the binding usage patterns.
9. //!
10. //! Runs under the pmon supervisor via a Python shim that execs this binary, so
11. //! `supervisorctl status xcvrd` reports RUNNING.
12. 
13. fn main() {
14.     xcvrd_rs::daemon::run();
15. }
16.

1. //! xcvrd-rs bootstrap library.
2. //!
3. //! This is the starting point the ReCodeAgent translation pipeline builds on. The
4. //! two environment bindings the daemon needs are already wired as dependencies, so
5. //! agents can `use` them directly and never re-solve interop:
6. //!
7. //!   - [`platform_bridge`] — the Python `sonic_platform` HAL (xcvr-emu) via PyO3.
8. //!     `Platform`/`Chassis`/`Sfp` expose `get_transceiver_info`, `get_change_event`,
9. //!     DOM/status, lpmode/reset, eeprom, … (CMIS decode stays in Python).
10. //!   - [`swss_common`] — STATE_DB (Redis) via the official sonic-net bindings.
11. //!     `DbConnector`, `Table`, `ProducerStateTable`, `SubscriberStateTable`, …
12. //!
13. //! [`env`] gives ready-made constructors ([`env::open_platform`],
14. //! [`env::open_state_db`]) so daemon code has one documented place to obtain a HAL
15. //! handle and a STATE_DB connection. Agents grow this module into the real
16. //! platform/DB layer as the milestones (see the repo README §5) require.
17. //!
18. //! Runnable demonstrations live in `examples/` (build with `cargo build
19. //! --examples`, or `bash tools/env_check.sh` to run them inside pmon):
20. //!   - `statedb_probe`   — STATE_DB round-trip via swss-common only.
21. //!   - `hal_to_statedb`  — the agent pattern: read a transceiver via the bridge,
22. //!                          then publish it to STATE_DB (what `SfpStateUpdateTask`
23. //!                          will do for real).
24. 
25. pub mod daemon;
26. pub mod env;
27.

1. //! Environment seed for the daemon: thin, documented constructors for the two
2. //! bindings so there is a single place to obtain a HAL handle and a STATE_DB
3. //! connection. The translation agents extend this into the real platform/DB layer
4. //! (per-port SFP handles, table helpers, publish/subscribe loops, …) as the
5. //! milestones grow — start here rather than calling the raw bindings ad hoc.
6. 
7. use platform_bridge::Platform;
8. use swss_common::DbConnector;
9. 
10. /// SONiC STATE_DB logical index (Redis db number).
11. pub const STATE_DB: i32 = 6;
12. 
13. /// SONiC CONFIG_DB logical index (Redis db number).
14. pub const CONFIG_DB: i32 = 4;
15. 
16. /// Redis unix socket path inside pmon (override with the `REDIS_SOCK` env var).
17. pub fn redis_sock() -> String {
18.     std::env::var("REDIS_SOCK").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/var/run/redis/redis.sock".to_string())
19. }
20. 
21. /// Open the transceiver HAL: PyO3 → `sonic_platform.Platform().get_chassis()`.
22. ///
23. /// Constructing the platform triggers the emulator `List()` RPC (falls back to
24. /// `XCVR_EMU_NUM_SFPS` placeholders if the emulator isn't up yet — same as the
25. /// Python daemon at start-up). Hand the returned [`Platform`] out and call
26. /// `num_sfps()` / `sfp(i)` / `get_change_event(timeout_ms)`.
27. pub fn open_platform() -> platform_bridge::Result<Platform> {
28.     Platform::new()
29. }
30. 
31. /// Open a STATE_DB connection over the Redis unix socket.
32. ///
33. /// Use the returned [`DbConnector`] for direct hash access (`hset`/`hgetall`/…),
34. /// or wrap it in a `swss_common::Table` / `ProducerStateTable` for table-scoped
35. /// writes like `TRANSCEIVER_INFO`.
36. pub fn open_state_db() -> swss_common::Result<DbConnector> {
37.     DbConnector::new_unix(STATE_DB, redis_sock(), 0)
38. }
39. 
40. /// Open a CONFIG_DB connection over the Redis unix socket (for the PORT table /
41. /// logical↔physical port mapping).
42. pub fn open_config_db() -> swss_common::Result<DbConnector> {
43.     DbConnector::new_unix(CONFIG_DB, redis_sock(), 0)
44. }
45.

230.         if port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_ADD:
231.             self._handle_port_add(port_change_event)
232.         elif port_change_event.event_type == PortChangeEvent.PORT_REMOVE:
233.             self._handle_port_remove(port_change_event)

235.     def _handle_port_add(self, port_change_event):
236.         port_name = port_change_event.port_name
237.         self.logical_port_list.append(port_name)

239.         if port_change_event.port_index not in self.physical_to_logical:
240.             self.physical_to_logical[port_change_event.port_index] = [port_name]

1. #!/bin/bash
2. # Build the xcvrd-rs crate for pmon, inside the Debian-13 build container.
3. # Runs on the sonic-dev host (has docker + internet). Produces a glibc-2.41
4. # binary that links libpython3.13 (for the PyO3 platform-bridge).
5. #
6. # Usage: build_crate.sh <CRATE_DIR>
7. set -uo pipefail
8. CRATE_DIR="${1:-$HOME/recode/crate}"
9. IMG=recode-rust-build
10. HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11. 
12. if ! docker image inspect "$IMG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
13.   echo "[build] image $IMG missing; build it first: docker build -t $IMG -f dut/Dockerfile.build ." >&2
14.   exit 2
15. fi
16. 
17. # Ensure libswsscommon.so is staged for the linker. xcvrd-rs will depend on
18. # swss-common (STATE_DB) once the agents wire it in; staging now is harmless for
19. # the current skeleton and makes that build "just work".
20. bash "$HERE/ensure_swsslib.sh" || true
21. 
22. echo "[build] cargo build --release in $IMG (crate=$CRATE_DIR)"
23. # Mount the crate; keep target/ in it so the cargo cache persists across runs.
24. # Mount swsslib + set RUSTFLAGS so `-lswsscommon` resolves (SWSS_COMMON_REPO +
25. # BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS are baked into the image).
26. # --network host so cargo can fetch crates.io + git deps (pyo3, swss-common, ...).
27. docker run --rm --network host \
28.   -v "$CRATE_DIR":/src -v "$HOME/recode/swsslib":/swsslib -w /src \
29.   -e RUSTFLAGS="-L native=/swsslib" \
30.   "$IMG" \
31.   cargo build --release --bin xcvrd-rs
32. rc=$?
33. BIN="$CRATE_DIR/target/release/xcvrd-rs"
34. if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
35.   echo "[build] FAILED (rc=$rc, binary present: $([ -x "$BIN" ] && echo yes || echo no))" >&2
36.   exit 2
37. fi
38. echo "[build] OK -> $BIN"

# Planner working notes (xcvrd Python -> Rust)

Working copy: `pipeline/crate` (immutable source: `crate/`). Edit ONLY the working copy.

## Deliverables
1. `pipeline/crate/xcvrd-rs/src/**` compilable skeleton (stubs + trait seams + mocks).
2. `pipeline/plan.json` (fragments, name_mapping, skeleton, milestones M0-M6).

## Seams (Part B enablement)
- `hal.rs`: `trait SfpApi`, `trait Hal` (assoc type Sfp). Real `PlatformHal`/`PlatformSfp` wrap `platform_bridge`.
- `statedb.rs`: `trait TableApi`, `trait StateDb` (assoc type Table). Real `SwssStateDb`/`SwssTable` over `swss_common::DbConnector` (key = `<table>|<lport>`).
- `mock.rs` (#[cfg(test)]): `MockHal`/`MockSfp`, `MockStateDb`/`MockTable` (direct port of mock_swsscommon.Table; shared Rc<RefCell> store).

## Layout mirror (python -> rust)
xcvrd.py -> xcvrd/{mod.rs, sfp_state_update.rs}; sff_mgr.py -> sff_mgr.rs;
cmis/cmis_manager_task.py -> cmis/{mod.rs,cmis_manager_task.rs};
dom/dom_mgr.py -> dom/{mod.rs,dom_mgr.rs}; dom/utilities/** mirrored;
xcvrd_utilities/** mirrored (common, port_event_helper, sfp_status_helper, xcvr_table_helper, media_settings_parser, optics_si_parser, utils).

## Build

I'm also looking at port event handling with classes for tracking port changes, mapping logical to physical ports, and subscribing to configuration updates. Now examining the transceiver table helper that manages interface, status, DOM, and threshold tables, along with utility functions for checking transceiver presence, flat memory support, and low-power mode status. Looking at the test cases from Part B that verify the core functionality—specifically tests for posting SFP info to the database, handling cases where transceivers aren't present, and combining SFP info with DOM threshold data.

Then there are tests for initializing port SFP status tables and handling scenarios where no physical ports exist, along with tests for the SfpStateUpdateTask that map events from change notifications and handle SFP insertion and removal events. The task worker test is more complex and needs to be split into smaller tests, while the port change event handler and EEPROM retry logic can be translated directly from the existing tests.

Continuing with wrapper functions for checking if components are replaceable, getting transceiver information and types, and retrieving SFP error descriptions and change events. I'm also looking at tests for detecting error conditions in ports and identifying problematic SFP statuses, with some flag metadata and DOM flag tests deferred to later phases.

For the mock objects, I'm converting the Python mock implementations to Rust, replacing MockChassis and MockSfp with their Rust equivalents, and translating the mock table implementations as well.
